subject: Cedar Analytics — request for SLA appendix + order form language
messages:
From: Li Wei <li.wei@cedaranalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cedaranalytics.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA appendix + order form language for enterprise MSA/SOW

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up with a formal request: Cedar will need an attachable SLA appendix (MSA/SOW) and clarified order-form language that explicitly calls out availability and latency commitments for the inference endpoints used by our core product.

Key asks from our side:
- Availability: target uptime threshold and credit schedule; Cedar's procurement team is pushing for 99.99% for core inference endpoints across us-west and us-east (primary + regional failover).
- Latency: p95 and p99 commitments for typical request size (we expect 64–512 token calls); we need firm numbers and a definition of measurement windows (rolling monthly).
- Evidence: telemetry/monitoring export or SOC/attestation points that show per-route uptime and latency (30–90 day retention for audit).
- Failover: behaviour on regional outages — Do you provide automatic routing to secondary region? What SLO applies during cross-region failover windows?
- Order form language: we need a single-paragraph insert we can include in the order form to lock the commitments and reference the SLA appendix.

I've attached a short redline doc with the procurement team's initial preferences (Cedar_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx). Can your legal/procurement team review and propose an addendum? We prefer tracked changes in a Word doc for turnaround.

Timing: procurement would like a first pass by end of week if possible; their internal review window is short.

Appreciate the help — if it makes sense I'm happy to run a 30-minute sync between our teams.

Thanks,
Li Wei
Senior Procurement Manager
Cedar Analytics

Adding technical detail from the runtime side — copying the pieces I'll include in the draft:

- Availability definition: We measure endpoint availability as successful TCP+TLS+HTTP 200-ish responses to inference route health-checks and production requests, aggregated to per-route availability. Downtime is defined as > 5 consecutive minutes of failed response checks unless caused by scheduled maintenance.
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day measurement for uptime percentage; credits calculated monthly.
- Latency commitments: p95 and p99 measured on server-side processing time excluding network transit, using a rolling 30-day window. For 64 token requests we can commit to p95 < 120ms, p99 < 400ms on dedicated capacity. For 512 token requests p95 < 220ms, p99 < 950ms on dedicated plans — these are baseline numbers and depend on reserved capacity size.
- Regional failover: Automatic smart routing is available. During cross-region failover we treat requests routed to a secondary region as served; the SLOs above apply to protected (“core”) endpoints only when both regions are healthy. We propose a carveout credit structure for full-region outages lasting more than 30 minutes.
- Telemetry: We can provide per-route latency and availability exports (CSV/JSON) with 90-day retention on request; longer retention available as an add-on.

I'll attach a short technical appendix to the SLA draft with the exact metric names, example queries, and the credit schedule math.

Happy to talk through this on the sync.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Mina/Ben,

Thanks for the fast responses and the proposed numbers — helpful. A few clarifications and Cedar's feedback after an internal review:

1) Availability: Cedar will accept a draft with 99.99% for core endpoints, provided the credit schedule is scaled and clears up the treatment for partial-region impact vs total-region outage. We need explicit language for sustained cross-region failover (we want to ensure credits are not waived if failover is due to Redwood capacity constraints).

2) Latency: The numbers you provided are in line with expectations. Procurement wants p99 for 512-token calls to be explicitly called out (we will run a pilot and confirm typical token distributions). We'll want to lock those numbers for the first 12 months with a review clause at renewal.

3) Evidence & telemetry: 90-day export is OK; procurement prefers a daily CSV delivery to a secure S3 bucket or a shared Drive link for audit. Is S3 delivery supported?

4) Order form language: procurement asks for a single binding clause that references the Sylvia SLA Appendix (name placeholder) and states that the appendix controls to the extent of any conflict. Please include the exact clause so their legal can move faster.

Attached our annotated redlines for the SLA (Cedar_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx) with a few suggested edits on credits and force majeure carveouts.

We can do the sync today at 10am PT; I've scheduled for that slot — invite sent.

Regards,
Li

Li,

Appreciate the marked-up redlines and the quick sync today. Next steps and what we agreed on the call:

- Redwood legal (cc Kimberly) will finalize a tracked-changes SLA addendum that:
  * Commits to 99.99% monthly uptime for designated core inference endpoints with a graduated credit schedule for partial vs full-region outages.
  * Commits to the agreed latency bands (p95/p99) for 64 and 512 token buckets on Dedicated plans for the first 12 months, with a renewal review clause.
  * Defines measurement windows as rolling 30-day windows and telemetry aggregation semantics.
- Telemetry delivery: Redwood will deliver daily CSV exports to a secured S3 bucket (we will send a presigned upload flow or IAM role if Cedar prefers). 90-day retention by default; extended retention available as paid add-on.
- Order form clause (proposed language below) to be included verbatim in the order form:

  "The Redwood SLA Appendix attached hereto (the 'SLA Appendix') sets forth availability and latency commitments applicable to Customer's designated inference endpoints. In the event of any conflict between this Order Form and the SLA Appendix, the terms of the SLA Appendix will govern solely with respect to Availability and Latency obligations."

- Kimberly will post the final tracked Word doc (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_vA.docx with redlines) to the shared HubSpot deal record and route via DocuSign once Cedar confirms redlines.

I attached the initial tracked Order Form that includes the above clause and the credit table Ben proposed (Redwood_OrderForm_TrackedChanges.pdf). Please review and let us know any final edits; our legal team will aim to get a final signable package by Monday.

Thanks everyone — good progress.

Best,
